\section*{Question 2}

The figure above shows the graphs of the circles \(x^{2}+y^{2}=2\) and \((x-1)^{2}+y^{2}=1\). The graphs intersect at the points \((1,1)\) and (1,-1). Let \(R\) be the shaded region in the first quadrant bounded by the two circles and the \(x\)-axis.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Set up an expression involving one or more integrals with respect to \(x\) that represents the area of \(R\).
\item[(b)] Set up an expression involving one or more integrals with respect to \(y\) that represents the area of \(R\).
\item[(c)] The polar equations of the circles are \(r=\sqrt{2}\) and \(r=2 \cos \theta\), respectively. Set up an expression involving one or more integrals with respect to the polar angle \(\theta\) that represents the area of \(R\).
\item[(a)] Area \(=\int_{0}^{1} \sqrt{1-(x-1)^{2}} d x+\int_{1}^{\sqrt{2}} \sqrt{2-x^{2}} d x\)
OR
\[
\text { Area }=\frac{1}{4}\left(\pi \cdot 1^{2}\right)+\int_{1}^{\sqrt{2}} \sqrt{2-x^{2}} d x
\]
\item[(b)] Area \(=\int_{0}^{1}\left(\sqrt{2-y^{2}}-\left(1-\sqrt{1-y^{2}}\right)\right) d y\)
\item[(c)] Area \(=\int_{0}^{\pi / 4} \frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{2})^{2} d \theta+\int_{\pi / 4}^{\pi / 2} \frac{1}{2}(2 \cos \theta)^{2} d \theta\)
OR
\[
\text { Area }=\frac{1}{8} \pi(\sqrt{2})^{2}+\int_{\pi / 4}^{\pi / 2} \frac{1}{2}(2 \cos \theta)^{2} d \theta
\]
\end{itemize}
\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integrand for larger circle } \\ 1: \text { integrand or geometric area } \\ \quad \text { for smaller circle } \\ 1: \text { limits on integral(s) }\end{array}\right.\)
Note: < -1 > if no addition of terms
